title: The same half-covered edge, encoded at two resolutions, is not a difference
why: Averaging straight alpha and compositing the ground afterwards do not commute, so the same picture scored differently depending only on how its exporter encoded a partly covered pixel. The score plane averages premultiplied colour, which makes the two orderings the one expression `mean(a·c) + g·(1 − mean(a))` — and is what `drawImage` produced before the portable kernel replaced it, since a canvas downscales premultiplied.
